A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ViBiDSampler and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably despite expanded appendices and repagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original DAVIS/Pexels evaluations, computational measurements, guidance ablations, and qualitative interpolation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds PSNR/SSIM evaluations, guided-baseline comparisons, and an SVD-versus-SVD-XT ablation in Tables 4–6.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain sequential forward/backward denoising, intervening re-noising, temporal reversal, and the same DDS/CFG++ guidance. Renaming and expanded equations do not establish a changed procedure. The new SVD-XT disclosure identifies the implementation rather than documenting a replacement of the main method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate two-keyframe interpolation on DAVIS and Pexels and retain the identical/dynamic boundary demonstrations. The additional experiments use existing coverage; text-conditioned generation appears only as future work.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FILM, TRF, DynamiCrafter, and Generative Inbetweening. New Table 5 additionally evaluates TRF and Generative Inbetweening enhanced with CFG++ and DDS against the proposed method, extending the comparator configurations without replacing the original comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 adds PSNR/SSIM evaluation against ground-truth frames. B.2 adds controls applying guidance to competing samplers, and B.4 compares SVD backbones. The original 100 DAVIS videos, 45 Pexels videos, and 25-step-per-direction Euler sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's within-method guidance and guidance-scale ablations, v3 tests whether CFG++/DDS also benefit TRF and Generative Inbetweening (B.2, Table 5) and whether results depend on SVD versus SVD-XT (B.4, Table 6). These substantially extend analyses distinguishing the sampler's contribution from guidance and backbone effects.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new tables continue reporting single values without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their values, while Tables 4–6 substantially expand results with distortion metrics, guided-baseline outcomes, and backbone comparisons. For example, Pexels FVD changes from 880.97 to 778.69 when guidance is added to TRF, but from 746.26 to 747.95 for Generative Inbetweening. The backbone ablation reports FVD 608.07 for SVD versus 452.34 for SVD-XT. These are newly reported experimental comparisons, not performance gains between paper versions.

T1.justification: Most equation edits merely expand existing Euler updates or rename denoised estimates. However, v3 Equation (9) omits time-reversal primes on its right-hand side, unlike v2's backward update and the retained algorithm listings. This introduces a local inconsistency in the mathematical specification; no new theorem, assumption, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free bidirectional sampling with DDS/CFG++, mitigation of off-manifold artifacts, and efficient high-quality interpolation. The headline claim of generating 25 frames at 1024 × 576 in 195 seconds on a 3090 GPU is unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation connecting re-noising to avoiding mode collapse, hypotheses about guidance compatibility and interference across samplers, and an explicit text-conditioning limitation. B.1 also interprets the new distortion results, but its claim of best PSNR/SSIM among generative baselines overlooks Generative Inbetweening's higher Pexels SSIM.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly specifies that the implementation uses SVD-XT, whereas v2 refers generally to SVD. B.2 adds a link to supplementary qualitative material. Existing hardware, sampling settings, motion bucket ID, decoding settings, and original access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work section and cited-work set are retained. Section 3.2 makes a limited positioning addition by explicitly describing DDS's original image inverse-problem setting and presenting its transfer to bounded video generation as a novel insight.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the guidance explanation, standardizes mathematical notation, renames the algorithm listings, and organizes the expanded Appendix B into six subsections. Affiliations, publication headers, and an acknowledgment are added or updated. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds compact Tables 4–6 and revises Figure 5's highlighting and enlarged crops, emphasizing frame I20 instead of I24. Figures 8–10 retain their content but move into B.6 after the additions. Other figure content and the original table structures are retained, with local layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The new guidance controls and backbone ablation strengthen attribution of the method's gains, while identifying SVD-XT improves reproducibility and the distortion metrics broaden evaluation. These benefits are tempered by B.1's incorrect best-SSIM claim: Generative Inbetweening scores 0.6334 on Pexels versus 0.5939 for the proposed method. Equation (9) also introduces inconsistent reversal notation, although the algorithms remain clear. Overall, the additional evidence provides a limited net improvement.
